sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Miami Lakes?
sections.html:
Miami Lakes is a planned town in northwest Miami-Dade County, and that planning shapes how its houses sell. The Town's FY2024-25 annual report puts the population near 31,240 and counts about 4,720 businesses inside roughly 6.5 square miles.

The Town incorporated on December 5, 2000. The report places it 16 miles north of Downtown Miami and about 10 miles from Miami International Airport, which is the commute story most buyers hear first. Its boundaries run from NW 170th Street and the Palmetto Expressway on the north to NW 138th Street on the south, and from NW 57th Avenue (Red Road) on the east to Interstate 75 on the west.

Because so much of the town sits inside one master plan, a seller here usually deals with a homeowners association, a lake or canal frontage question, or a special taxing district earlier than sellers in older grid-pattern suburbs.

sections.h2: Why does the master plan of Miami Lakes matter when I sell?
sections.html:
The layout traces back to a dairy farm. The Town's history page says the Graham family began developing their dairy land more than 50 years ago and hired Lester Collins, a former dean of the Harvard School of Architecture, to draw a master plan for the original 3,000 acres.

That plan produced winding streets, cul-de-sacs, 23 lakes, parks and separate business parks. Buyers see this on a drive-by, so curb appeal, tree condition and the state of the swale matter more than usual. The annual report adds that light industrial and office parks take up about 13 percent of the Town and lakes and canals about 11 percent.

  • Housing ranges from medium-density multifamily to large waterfront single-family homes, with many lakefront townhouse communities.
  • The town is described as mostly low density, with a Town Center and parks spread between neighborhoods.
  • The Town's businesses employ about 30,000 people, and only 12 percent of those workers live in Miami Lakes.

sections.h2: What local services and projects could affect my Miami Lakes house?
sections.html:
Fire and rescue calls in Miami Lakes are answered by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, mainly from the Miami Lakes station and the Miami Lakes West station, which together handled about 89 percent of responses in fiscal 2025. The report counts 3,546 emergency calls to the Town that year.

Drainage work is the item a seller is most likely to notice. The report lists finished projects such as Canal Bank Stabilization Phase III, the Francesca Mary and Loch Lomond drainage improvements, and a long list of neighborhood drainage jobs in progress, including Royal Oaks additions and West Lakes Phase IV. If your street shows up in a project list, tell the buyer what was done and ask the Town for the project status in writing.

The Town also runs the FreeBee on-demand ride service, which gave more than 28,564 rides in the year, and it launched a Vision Zero plan for road safety. The Parks and Recreation section mentions automated gate arms and guardhouse work in the Town's special taxing districts, so a house inside a guarded district carries extra costs a buyer will ask about.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when a Miami Lakes house is sold?
sections.html:
Florida charges a documentary stamp tax on deeds, and Miami-Dade County is the one county with a different schedule. The Department of Revenue prints the rates below. The same page says every party to the document is liable regardless of who agrees to pay, so the contract should say who pays.

Deed documentary stamp tax as printed by the Florida Department of Revenue
PlaceRate on a deed
Counties other than Miami-Dade70 cents per $100 or portion thereof
Miami-Dade County60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax
Surtax exceptionNot due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling

Miami Lakes has many lakefront townhouses and multifamily units, so ask the title company which line applies to your property type. The clerk of the court collects the tax at recording, and the clerk also charges recording fees by page under section 28.24.

Property tax is a separate bill. The Town's annual report charts FY2024 adopted millage rates for Miami-Dade municipalities and shows Miami Lakes at 2.0732 mills. The Town also launched a web-based millage calculator so residents can compare current and prior year taxes. Millage is one slice of the bill, because the county, school board and special districts add their own.

sections.h2: How do Florida property tax dates and homestead rules affect a Miami Lakes sale?
sections.html:
Assessment happens each January 1, which means the owner on that date is who the county assesses for the year, even if the house sells in spring. Tax bills go out in November, and the state lists discounts of 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1.

  • Homestead applications go to the Miami-Dade property appraiser by March 1, using Form DR-501.
  • Homestead status ends if the home is rented or is no longer your permanent residence.
  • The Save Our Homes cap limits yearly increases for homesteaded property, and a sale resets the property to just value the next January 1.
  • A TRIM notice arrives in August, and a value petition must reach the clerk within 25 days of that notice.

The buyer's first tax bill may be far higher than the one you paid. Ask the title agent to prorate the current year and to hold back enough for the November bill if it has not been issued.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a Miami Lakes house quickly?
sections.html:
Three routes are open to a Miami Lakes owner: an agent listing, a sale you market yourself, or an investor's cash bid. Each one swaps speed for price in a different way. A listing reaches the most buyers but brings showings, inspection requests and a loan approval period. A cash offer from an investor can close faster, and the buyer usually takes the house as it is, but the price is typically lower than a retail sale.

  • Listing: exposure to financed buyers, repairs and concessions negotiated after inspection.
  • For sale by owner: you save the agent fee but handle contracts, disclosures and showings yourself.
  • Cash buyer: fewer contingencies and a closing date you choose, with a discount for speed.

Gather written offers, ask each bidder who covers title work and stamps, and have an attorney or title company read the contract before you sign.

sections.h2: What if the Miami Lakes house is behind on payments or inherited?
sections.html:
A lender who files foreclosure must go to court, and after a final judgment the clerk sells the property at a public sale not less than 20 days or more than 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period. The high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and objections to a sale must be filed within 10 days of the certificate of sale. Selling before that date lets you keep any equity.

For an inherited house, summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the person has been dead more than two years. Creditors have until the later of three months after the first notice publication or 30 days after being served to file claims. Florida repealed its estate tax for deaths after 2004, so no state estate tax return is needed.

If someone is living in the house without a lease, section 82.036 lets an owner file a verified complaint so the sheriff can remove unlawful occupants when strict conditions are met. A tenant with a lease is a different matter, and Florida requires a three-day written notice for unpaid rent before an eviction suit.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Miami Lakes?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a few weeks if title is clear, while a listing with a financed buyer typically takes longer because of inspection, appraisal and lender steps. Title issues, liens and homeowners association approvals can slow any route.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Miami Lakes deed?
faqs.a: The contract decides who pays, but the state says all parties to the document are liable. Miami-Dade County uses 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, with the surtax not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Does a sale reset my property tax assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. A change of ownership resets the property to just value the next January 1, so the new owner does not inherit the Save Our Homes cap. Spousal transfers and some transfers at death are exceptions.

faqs.q: Can a house in a guarded Miami Lakes district be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, but the buyer will see the district assessment and any gate or guardhouse costs on the tax bill. Ask the Town and the Miami-Dade tax collector for the current amounts before you set a price.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after a Miami Lakes sale?
faqs.a: Recording happens at the Miami-Dade clerk of the court, and the clerk takes the stamp tax and the per-page charges in the same step. A title company normally submits the paperwork for you.
